title: Harutyunyan's acyclic-set conjecture for planar oriented graphs
statement: Let an **oriented graph** be a digraph without loops and multiple arcs, and let an **acyclic set** be a set of vertices inducing a subgraph with no directed cycles. **Harutyunyan's conjecture.** Every planar oriented graph of order $n$ has an acyclic set of size at least $\frac{3n}{5}$. The conjecture is refuted by the paper's construction of oriented planar graphs whose maximum acyclic set has size at most $\lceil \frac{n+1}{2} \rceil$.
source_name: Kolja Knauer, Petru Valicov and Paul S. Wenger, “Planar digraphs without large acyclic sets”, arXiv:1504.06726 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.06726

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2015). “However, the following remains open: [Albertson and Berman ] Every simple undirected planar graph of order $n$ has an induced forest of order at least $\frac{n}{2}$.”
